<details open>

ggml-openvino: fix OpenVINO CI, minor fixes and optimizations (#32590)

* ggml-openvino: round the GPU KV length up to a power of two

Review notes (follow-ups, not blocking):
- convert_ggml_input_to_ov pads the KQ mask into a std::vector and then
  copies it into the ov::Tensor. Writing the padded rows straight into
  padded.data() avoids the second allocation and copy (up to 16 MB per
  call at a 16K context).
- The padding is skipped when the mask is not contiguous, and the KV
  inputs are then sliced to more rows than the mask has columns. Masks
  are always contiguous today; a GGML_ASSERT would make that explicit.
- compute_llm_params reads GGML_OPENVINO_STATEFUL_EXECUTION directly;
  is_stateful_enabled() is local to ggml-openvino.cpp.

* ggml-openvino: Optimize model recompiles of prefill stage

Optimize the model recompiles of prefill stage when attended size
changed between prompts. This can save model recompile time for
llama-bench and llama-server.

* ggml-openvino: Optimize model recompiles of prefill stage

Optimize the model recompiles of prefill stage when attended size
changed between prompts. This can save model recompile time for
llama-bench and llama-server.

* ggml-openvino: Remove solution C and keep A as default

* ggml-openvino: match the output count before reusing a compiled NPU prefill

The static prefill model has a fixed inp_out_ids shape [1,1,1,output_len].
The new reuse check compared only the attention sizes, so llama-perplexity,
which alternates 1 and 512 outputs per ubatch, reused the model compiled
for 512 outputs on a 1-output ubatch and failed with "got [1,1,1,1]
expecting [1,1,1,512]". Store the output count of the cached prefill
model and require it to match.

* ggml-openvino: Fix LFM2 context create on GPU and DSpar

items.name: b12549
items.body:
<details open>

llama: fixes for Inkling 2 attention mask (#32429)

* llama : give Inkling2 its own relative-position attention input

The Inkling2 graph built its flash attention mask from the hybrid iswa
input and passed it to build_attn through a new kq_mask argument. That
argument let a caller pair its own dense mask with the kv_rows of
llm_graph_input_attn_kv_iswa, whose mask follows the per-sequence cell
lists whenever kv_rows is enabled.

Add llm_graph_input_attn_rel_pos instead. It owns dense KQ masks and the
query-to-cell distances, fills both from the same cells, and its
build_attn overload adds the per-head bias to its own mask and never
passes kv_rows. The iswa build_attn is back to its previous signature;
its body moves to build_attn_iswa_impl, which both overloads call.

Inkling2 now folds the per-query sink into the bias with and without
flash attention, so build_attn_mha no longer needs the per-query sink
path.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* inkling2 : make the expert weight scale and final logit softcap optional

Load both keys as optional and skip them when they are zero, as other
models do, instead of rejecting zero at load.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* llama : build kv_rows masks for the hybrid iswa memory

llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_iswa checked its masks with
can_reuse_attn_mask, which expects kv_rows whenever they are enabled,
but built them dense. With a unified cache and flash attention the
check always failed, and hybrid iswa models (LFM2, LFM3, Inkling2)
never reused a graph. Build the masks with build_attn_inp_attn_mask,
like the plain iswa input.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* llama : make the relative-position input a hybrid iswa input

Address review: llm_graph
